subject.title: Automatic Anthropic model catalog: live Models API discovery + capability-driven contracts

question: For a live-discovered Anthropic model without complete generation-specific request-contract coverage, should OpenClaw hide it, expose it with capability-derived best-effort behavior, or expose it as a clearly degraded preview?
rationale: This choice determines whether discovery can safely ship independently and defines the user-facing compatibility contract for newly released models; source inspection cannot select that product policy.

options.title: Gate uncontracted models
options.body: Keep live discovery limited to rows whose required request semantics are covered, so the catalog never advertises a model likely to fail at runtime.

options.title: Use capability-derived best effort
options.body: Expose new models when published capabilities cover the generic contract, accepting that undocumented provider quirks may still require follow-up fixes.

options.title: Expose as preview
options.body: Show incomplete rows with an explicit degraded or preview state so advanced users can opt in while preserving a visible warning.

recommendation.title: Gate uncontracted models
recommendation.body: Keep live discovery limited to rows whose required request semantics are covered, so the catalog never advertises a model likely to fail at runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently implemented the related Anthropic model-contract update and framed the concrete policy alternatives in this issue.
